content.text: I have enough to conclude. No exclusivity or sole-source obligation binds Sanofi anywhere in the agreement.

input.quote: Except pursuant to or as expressly permitted by this Agreement, RevMed shall not, shall cause its Affiliates not to, conduct or agree to conduct, outside of the Collaboration, on its own or together with one or more Third Parties, the Research, Development or Commercialization of any product that contains a SHP2 Inhibitor
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no exclusivity, "sole supplier" or requirements obligation on Sanofi, so the rule sits at the preferred position. All exclusivity runs in our favour: Section 3.1(a) grants Sanofi an exclusive licence (even as to RevMed) under the RevMed Licensed Technology, and Section 3.5(a) is a non-compete binding RevMed and its Affiliates with respect to SHP2 Inhibitor products — a benefit to us that we do not flag. On sourcing, Article VII contains no obligation for Sanofi to procure solely from RevMed; Section 7.1 gives Sanofi oversight of registrational and commercial Manufacture, Section 7.2 requires RevMed to transfer Manufacturing Know-How and even to support Sanofi in establishing its own Third Party supply agreements, and Section 7.3 only contemplates a negotiated Supply Agreement where one Party in fact manufactures for the other. Section 12.2(d) (Termination for Competing Product of Sanofi) is worth noting but is not an exclusivity covenant: it does not prohibit Sanofi from developing a Competing Product; it only gives RevMed a conditional termination right (limited to the pre-Registrational Clinical Trial window and subject to a Sanofi cure election). We record this as a residual soft restraint rather than a deviation, and no redline is proposed.
